title: Per-device rate limiting on telemetry ingestion
name: Telemetry ingest limiter

questions.prompt: Is there a defect in how this code enforces the per-device ingestion limit? If so, mark the line(s) where it is; otherwise answer that there is none.
A device stops sending for longer than idleEviction and then resumes. What does the limiter do for that device?
choices: It rejects the first request because its bucket expired in an invalid state
It creates a fresh full bucket on the next call, which is equivalent to what the refill would have produced anyway
It restores the old token count from before the pause, so the device keeps any earlier debt
It throws, because Caffeine entries cannot be re-created after expiry

questions.prompt: The service runs as 6 identical instances behind a round-robin load balancer. What is the effective limit for one device?
choices: Exactly readingsPerSecond, because Bucket4j coordinates across JVMs automatically
Exactly readingsPerSecond, because Caffeine caches are shared per host
Up to roughly 6 x readingsPerSecond, since each instance keeps its own in-memory bucket for the device
readingsPerSecond / 6, because the capacity is split across instances

questions.prompt: Two requests from the same device arrive at the same instant on different threads while the bucket holds exactly one token and the consumed amount is 1. What happens?
choices: Exactly one tryConsumeAndReturnRemaining call succeeds; the other gets a probe with the wait time for refill
Both succeed, because the cache lookup and the consume are separate steps
Both are rejected, because Caffeine locks the entry while computing it
One succeeds and the other blocks until the bucket refills
